key_insight: Detonation-sprayed hydroxyapatite coatings improved titanium wear resistance, with the best tribological performance at O₂/C₂H₂ ratios of 3.0 and 3.3.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing the spray gas ratio could improve the durability of coated titanium implants under physiological conditions.
method: Deposit hydroxyapatite on Grade 2 titanium at O₂/C₂H₂ ratios of 2.6–3.7.
Characterize coating phases using X-ray diffraction.
Evaluate friction and wear under dry conditions and in Ringer’s solution.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports predominantly hydroxyapatite with partial α-tricalcium phosphate formation, improved wear resistance versus uncoated titanium, and lowest wear volumes at ratios of 3.0 and 3.3.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical wear results or biological validation, so improved osseointegration remains unconfirmed.
paper_title: STUDY OF TRIBOLOGICAL PROPERTIES OF BIOCOATINGS BY DETONATION SPRAYING METHOD
